selected_primary_idea.title: FateLedger: A Multi-Scale Cosmic-Fate Falsifiability Atlas
selected_primary_idea.summary: An assumption-aware framework that maps model family and finite-redshift evidence to a bounded background-fate status, a separately reported vacuum-stability status, and a testable future-discriminator plan.
selected_primary_idea.research_object: Late-time background expansion and logically separate false-vacuum transition risks.
mechanism: Attach a domain and asymptotic-continuation card to every dark-energy or modified-gravity model.
Map the declared continuation to H(a), a defined fate event, and a time integral only when mathematically well defined.
Evaluate observable likelihoods and posterior-predictive differences without claiming data beyond the observed interval.
Emit an independent vacuum-status panel with its own particle-physics assumptions.
Return an identifiability label and planned discriminator instead of forcing a time forecast.

hypotheses.statement: Assumption cards reduce unsupported future-fate assertions from finite-redshift fits.
hypotheses.falsification: If carded and uncarded analyses make the same rate of unsupported asymptotic claims under blind review, the card has no demonstrated value.

hypotheses.statement: Cross-probe predictive checks separate a subset of fate classes more robustly than single-probe fits.
hypotheses.falsification: If the combined analysis gives no better calibrated separation or merely reproduces one probe's systematic bias, the integration claim fails.

hypotheses.statement: Separate ledgers prevent expansion and vacuum-decay evidence from being logically conflated.
hypotheses.falsification: If a source-audited single-ledger protocol has equal contradiction and provenance error rates, separation has no demonstrated advantage.

hypotheses.statement: A declared non-identifiability output is the correct result when accessible observables cannot distinguish allowed asymptotic continuations.
hypotheses.falsification: If an independent observable set separates every retained continuation at the pre-registered criterion, non-identifiability should not be emitted.

expected_contribution: A traceable fate taxonomy with no forced universal end date.
A formal interface between observational constraints and future extrapolation.
A protocol for explaining what a new cosmological measurement can and cannot discriminate.

competitive_ideas.title: Redshift-to-Recollapse Forecast Ladder
competitive_ideas.reason_not_primary: Focuses on a single fate route and does not natively separate vacuum stability.

competitive_ideas.title: Bayesian Future-Continuation Ensemble
competitive_ideas.reason_not_primary: Useful method but prone to prior-dominated apparent certainty unless embedded in a broader audit protocol.

high_risk_ideas.title: Laboratory-Analog Vacuum-Decay Calibration Bridge
high_risk_ideas.risk: Analog systems do not directly measure a cosmological vacuum lifetime.

rejected_ideas.title: Universal Doomsday Clock
rejected_ideas.rejection_reason: Violates the Survey evidence boundary by combining conditional, noncommensurate mechanisms into one asserted time.

debate_summary.primary_strength: Transforms a vague endpoint question into falsifiable, source-constrained inference tasks.
debate_summary.primary_objection: Labels can inherit model and prior dependence.
debate_summary.guardrail: Pre-register continuation classes, show sensitivity analysis, and permit unresolved results.
